newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea probes bankers in Hanbo Loan scandal.
newsitem.headline: South Korea probes bankers in Hanbo Loan scandal.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors interrogated the heads of two leading local banks and a former president of a state bank Tuesday over a loan scandal surrounding insolvent Hanbo Steel Co.

Senior prosecutor Choi Byung-koog said Sheen Kwang-shik of Korea First Bank, Woo Chan-mok of Cho Hung Bank and Lee Hyung-koo, former chief of the state-run Korea Development Bank, were summoned to his Central Investigation Department.
"They are now being questioned over various suspicions." Choi told reporters.

Prosecution officials said the bankers would be questioned on whether they received commissions in return for offering huge loans to Hanbo Steel, the country's second-largest steelmaker. The bankers would also be asked whether they had faced pressure from politicians or government officials over the loans.

Hanbo Steel, flagship of the Hanbo Group, the 14th-largest conglomerate in South Korea, piled up about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions before it was declared insolvent on Jan. 23.
Finance Ministry officials said Korea First, Cho Hung and Korea Development were Hanbo Steel's three main creditor banks, with combined outstanding loans of 2.4 trillion won ($2.8 billion).
President Kim, who ordered a thorough probe into the loans last week, has called the scandal a typical example of corruption.
Prosecutors arrested Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo last Friday on charges of fraud and violating laws on checks and trust and savings companies.
